_comment: COLLECTIVE EDGE COLOR TOKENS v1.0. Mirrors snippets/palette.css exactly. Read by generators that cannot parse CSS: python-pptx, python-docx, matplotlib, reportlab, and any script emitting PPTX, DOCX, XLSX or PDF. Color only. Type values are NOT duplicated here; sizes, weights, leading, tracking and measure live in snippets/type-tokens.json, and the standard they come from is reference/type-system.md. Collective Edge has no hue of its own. White is the document surface, black is a band, and any color on a CE surface belongs to a partner.
name: Collective Edge

palette._comment: The raw brand palette, --ce-*. Collective Edge runs a grey ramp. White is the primary document surface; black is reserved for hero, divider and title surfaces.

black.use: Header bands, title slides, section dividers

mute.use: Dimmed non-text marks. 2.81:1 on white, so never text at any size

fog.use: The Edge wedge when CE stands alone. Never text

wedge._comment: The Edge wedge is the one part of the block mark that carries color, and that color is the PARTNER's. Every combination ships as a file. Never hand-recolor a mark.

foreground._comment: Semantic layer. Identical variable names in every brand, so a component written for one brand renders correctly in another with only palette.css swapped.

fg-4.use: Dimmed non-text marks. 2.81:1 on white, so never text. The dimmest text on white is #6E6E6E at 5.10:1

fg-accent.use: Brand-colored text. CE has no hue, so this is ink

bg-band.use: Header band, title slide, section divider

border-band-rule.use: Collective Edge ships no accent rule under its band. Apex uses gold here

status._comment: Identical in every brand so an operational signal never changes meaning between documents. Use functionally and sparingly, always paired with text or an arrow. A brand accent is never a status color.

diagramRoles._comment: Identical across every brand so a diagram reads the same regardless of whose document it sits in. Rectangles, 6px radius. Role is communicated by fill, never by shape. Never invent new hues for these roles. Each role names the text color that clears contrast on its own fill; measured, do not substitute.

decision.textRule: large or bold only, which is what a node label is. Never body copy on this fill.

warning.textRule: near-black, not white. White on this amber measures 2.70:1 and fails at every size.

data._comment: HOUSE DATA COLOUR v1.0. Identical in every kit and never forked. Mirrors snippets/data-color.css. A brand accent is never a series colour. Collective Edge is monochromatic, so slot 1 stays the house purple and is not remapped. Verify any set with scripts/validate-palette.py. Reasoning and measured numbers in reference/data-color.md.

series._comment: Categorical identity. Assign IN ORDER, never cycle, never generate a ninth. The order is the colour-blindness safety mechanism. Worst neighbouring pair: dE 9.8 simulated red-green and 22.3 normal vision on light, 14.5 and 26.4 on a dark ground. Cap of 3 on scatter, bubble, map and small multiples. Amber and orange sit below 3:1 on white and need a direct label or a table.

sequential._comment: Magnitude. One hue, light to dark, landing on Royal Purple at step 700. Steps 100 and 200 are for continuous scales only. Discrete ordered marks start at step 300. On a dark ground the anchor flips: the lightest step means the largest value.

diverging._comment: Polarity, distance above or below a baseline. Poles are red and teal, NOT red and green: red against green measures dE 5.5 under simulated deuteranopia and collapses into one colour. The midpoint is grey on purpose, because a hue there reads as a value rather than as no difference.

direction._comment: Is this good news. Colour follows favourable against unfavourable. It NEVER follows the arithmetic sign of the delta and never the direction of the arrow: a cost falling and transports rising are both favourable. Every value ships with an arrow or icon AND a word. The ink step is for text on the matching tint fill.

caution.note: Replaces --status-warn #B5821A for anything read as text. #B5821A measures 3.40:1 on white and was never legal at body size.

comparison._comment: The before-and-after chart, which is the most common chart in Royal material. Two tints of the brand hue is the defect this layer exists to fix: they are too close to separate, so the reader has to read the labels. An inert grey baseline against the accent reads instantly.

baseline.use: the prior period. Inert, and nothing to feel about it

comparison.variant: On a single-metric hero slide the result bar may take the direction colour instead. One slide, not a deck: if every bar is green, green stops carrying information.

chrome._comment: Recessive by policy. The grid is a hint, never a feature.

logos._comment: Ask for a role, never for a filename. Partner kits map the same five roles to different filenames. `-on-light` is the version to place ON a light background. Collective Edge ships no stacked lockup.

cobrandMarks._comment: The Edge wedge carries the partner's hue. Every combination ships as a file. Never hand-recolor a mark.

shadow._comment: The house is flat. Shadow signals elevation, never decoration.
